title: Camp Registration Five-Minute Drill
oneLiner: A parent war room for the January camp scramble: rank camps, prefill constraints, rehearse clicks, and keep backup childcare alive.
previewUrl: pending Stitch export in Phase B
targetUser: Working parents who need summer childcare but face expensive camps, tiny affordable capacity, and registration windows that sell out in minutes.
keyUx: Rank camps by schedule, price, commute, refund risk, and backup value; rehearse the registration sequence and produce a live fallback plan.
spread_trigger: Parents share the backup ladder with partners or grandparents before registration morning.
outputArtifact: registration drill card and backup ladder
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Camp Registration Five-Minute Drill" for Working parents who need summer childcare but face expensive camps, tiny affordable capacity, and registration windows that sell out in minutes.. The app is based on observed user pull from S10: Parents in high-cost areas report camps around $6,000 per child for 8 weeks and affordable YMCA slots selling out within minutes. S11: Summer activities increasingly run about $2,400 to $6,000 per child, making camp a childcare affordability problem. The app should use a Five-Minute Drill around the trigger moment "Rank camps by schedule, price, commute, refund risk, and backup value; rehearse the registration sequence and produce a live fallback plan." and make the first screen communicate "A parent war room for the January camp scramble: rank camps, prefill constraints, rehearse clicks, and keep backup childcare alive.". Build the core workflow around user-entered evidence and produce registration drill card and backup ladder. Required sections: Camp priority board; True weekly cost rows; Registration countdown drill; Document and payment checklist; Sibling and commute constraints; Backup care ladder; Family decision receipt. Emotional pressure to make visible: 사교육. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with steady family-planning interface with warm grouping, clear next actions, and low-panic countdown treatment. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like Five-Minute Drill.
